intro: Paired measurements should be compared within each example. An exact sign test asks whether positive and negative nonzero differences are balanced under a fair-sign null.
task: Compare the directions of paired changes using an exact two-sided sign test, excluding ties from the null trial count.
requirements: differences is a finite numeric vector of length at most 1000; positive means the first system did better, negative means the second did better.
Discard exact zero differences. Return integer wins, losses, ties and a two-sided p_value=min(1, 2*sum(comb(n,k), k=0..min(wins,losses))/2**n).
When all differences are ties or the vector is empty, return p_value 1. The test uses signs, not magnitudes, and assumes independent fair signs under the null.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Ties do not count as trials

hints.title: Remove ties from the trial count
hints.body: Zero differences are reported separately and excluded from the binomial null.

hints.title: Use the smaller tail
hints.body: The two-sided result doubles the lower tail through the less frequent sign, then caps it at one.

explanation: The exact sign test discards effect magnitudes and uses only the direction of nonzero paired changes. It avoids treating the two systems as independent samples.
A small p-value is evidence against the fair-sign null, not a measurement of practical benefit. Report the paired effect sizes alongside this sign-based diagnostic when interpreting real results.
